title: Ray Nance's long funeral and funeral services as shows
summary: Dance recounts delivering a eulogy at Nance's two-hour funeral and they agree services should not be vaudeville shows.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Yeah, well, there's a funny thing about that. I mean there is the New Orleans thing, and then there is like some of the funeral services they have in churches here, where people get up -- I mean you've been to some of them, and they sing and they play, and it's almost as though they were doing an audition.
You know, I mean that service for Ray Nance, did you go to that?

I missed Ray Nance -- you know, I didn't know Ray Nance had died until somebody called me on the contemplating Milt Hinton phone, and I was (unintelligible) and this regular Chicago bunch from the south side. The fellow in Denmark said, Hap, all those they get out-of Chicago's together. I said, yeah, I says, and I thought it was -- was whatchacallum.
Well, that funeral service went on for over two hours.

Yes, that was his wife. She asked for me to deliver the eulogy because I knew (unintelligible). Well, so when I get there, you know, I'd sort of written out something, not too long, Pastor Gense (unintelligible) had George Wein get up and deliver a sort of eulogy. Then he -- then I think someone in the middle of this thing -- I had to get up. Now, George Wein has already said some of the things I was going to say. It put me in a foolish position.

And then after I'd finished, after about a quarter of an hour of it, he reads out a sort of a eulogy that a priest in Montreal who knew Ray Nance (unintelligible), read this out. And in between we have girls singing, reading poems they had written and guys singing, and then -- I mean this went on for over two hours, and I think that's ridiculous. If anybody is seriously grieving for him, I mean you don't want to have to sit in that church for two hours. His mother was there. I mean how would she feel?

I know, I mean that's why I've been to those things masonic temples which have sort of done -- I mean Red Allen's funeral, which was a straight Catholic mass -- I mean to me that seemed right, but I don't particularly go for making a
I mean I think (unintelligible) to have somebody playing My Buddy and so forth at the end. I think that's very nice.
But I don't think you need about six or seven different acts.
No, no, definitely not. I know like at Zooty's funeral -- I forgot the trombone player's name, Milt Hampton, and they played a couple numbers. That was enough.
